issues.detail: The Greek phrase 'και ο καρπος υμων μενη' (and your fruit remains) is rendered in Vietnamese as 'hầu cho trái các ngươi còn lại; lại cũng cho...' The addition of 'lại cũng cho' (and also give/let) creates a grammatical disconnect. In the Greek, 'μενη' (remains) is the verb for the first clause, while the second clause starts with 'ινα ο τι αν αιτησητε' (so that whatever you ask). The Vietnamese translation makes it sound as if the fruit 'remains' and then 'gives' something, whereas the Greek structure is: [Fruit remains] AND [Whatever you ask... He gives].
